population.note: trace-overlap's members and order. Every answer reproduced its recorded tokens. The rows are every generated token and every question position of every answer; the overlap below lays them on trace-overlap's axis, one step per place, as sent-overlap did.

prediction_vs_result.predicted: At the places and matrices where the two groups diverge in what the matrix sends, the gap between their inputs is several times chance and the two halves agree. Where the groups follow each other, the input gap is close to chance.
observed: Where what a matrix sends diverges (57% of the places and matrices), the gap between the two groups' inputs is 3.7 times chance in both kinds of matrix (median), and two halves that share no answer agree on it at 0.79.
Where the groups follow each other in what the matrix sends, the input gap is 1.5 times chance (attention) and 1.4 (feed-forward), and the halves agree at 0.42 and 0.40.

By section of the path: before place 142 the input gap is 1.8 times chance (halves 0.70); places 142 to 304, 5.6 (0.85); places 305 to 456, 1.7 (0.39); places 457 to 479, 3.0 (0.64). The same shape as the turns and as what the matrices send.

By layer inside places 142 to 304 the input gap is 3.3 to 3.8 times chance in layer 0, about 5 in most layers, and largest in layers 14 to 23 (up to 10.5 at the attention output of layer 17). Before place 142 it is 1.7 to 2.1 at every depth.
An input gap above twice chance and a sending gap above twice chance fall on the same places and matrices: 53.7% of them have both, 3.7% only the sending, 3.2% only the input.
not_predicted: Where the groups follow each other the input gap is not at chance: it is about one and a half times chance and the halves agree at 0.4. A small recurring difference between the groups arrives at the matrices along the whole path, the question included in what is read.

failures_only.scope: Original model only. No edit in this run.

what_this_changes: A weight change can tell where it is from the input: where the patterns diverge, what arrives at each matrix differs between the groups by several times chance and recurs across answers, at every depth.

The difference in the inputs is the same difference the matrix sends on, as it has to be for a matrix that only multiplies. So the correction of one matrix changes what arrives at the next ones, and each matrix has to be fitted on what arrives after the earlier corrections are in the model.

Every answer's own rows are now on disk for both groups, at every token and at the question's positions, independent of any alignment. They are the token-by-token reference the path-ordered edit's baseline is compared with.
records: inputs/x-<kind>-<layer>.f32, state-<kind>-<layer>.f32, question-x-*, question-state-* and index.json (81 GB, not in Git; regenerated by `input_overlap record`)
